message: rebuild-from-events now lands db.sqlite at the CURRENT schema version: rebuildReadModelFromEvents (src/compact.js) stamps the 0.5 floor then runs migrate({quiet:true}) once inside the rebuild. Root cause of the post-compaction noise: writeViewSqlite builds the post-v0.7 shape but the stamp said 0.5, so EVERY next read re-ran and re-announced v0.6/v0.7. Merge 5a286a0; regression test test/rebuild-schema-current.test.js.

PATTERN: any code path that rewrites db.sqlite wholesale (writeViewSqlite targets) must bring it to the current schema version via migrate(db, {quiet:true}) — never hardcode a version number; the chain owns 'current' so a future v0.8 data backfill runs at rebuild time too.

atomicityOf (src/rubric.js) exempts messages with the '[rollup] ' prefix — a compaction rollup is multi-fact by construction, and doctor's non-atomic detector was telling the operator to split what compact just joined (3 loom triage candidates were the store's own rollups). generateRollupMessage dedupes exact-duplicate source messages (Set, first-seen order) — a runaway logger had appended one fact 45x to the loom store and the rollup text would have repeated it 45 times. All duplicate eids still land in the supersede's rolls_up; only the TEXT collapses. Near-duplicate REWORDINGS are NOT merged (semantic dedup is an LLM job, out of pebbl's deterministic scope). Merge 9b778b2.

handoff now REFUSES a detail-heavy handoff (>1200 chars of done+todo+blocked) that links neither --docs nor --no-doc — a write-time guard in handoff.js that fails BEFORE the insert, like malformedSummary. Fixed three scanner false-positive families in src/privacy-scan.js (commit 88c12d9, merge of fix/scanner-false-positives). (1) DTCG design-token paths: assignment-quoted/bare patterns were tripping on JSON schema entries like { "token": "color.primary" } because 'token' is an ASSIGNMENT_KEYWORD and the value is 12+ chars. Added DTCG_TOKEN_PATH_RE and skip captured values matching it in findTokens. Structural exemption, not a keyword allowlist - dot-notation identifiers are too narrow to be real secrets. (2) Language idioms for reading environment variables: CRED_PATH_PATTERNS[1] was matching property chains that contain neither a slash nor a hyphen. Tightened to require one of those in the matched token, so genuine hyphenated credential filenames and dotfile env paths under a directory still fire while the language idioms no longer do; the bare basename and the /root credential-dir shapes stay covered by patterns[0] and [2]. The exact regexes live in src/privacy-scan.js and are deliberately NOT copied here - a regex quoted in prose drifts from the one that runs, and quoting cred-path patterns makes the memory itself unpublishable. (3) Template placeholders fire and are intentionally left firing - a placeholder is ambiguous because it could expand to a real secret at runtime. Added 15 test fixtures to test/privacy-scan.test.js covering all three families. Full suite 605/0. Supersedes stash@{0} 'UNAUTHORIZED subagent edit 2026-07-28' (dropped after merge).

rubric migrations can now ADD a missing rule, not only edit an existing one: added the v0.7 step that inserts the steering rule when absent. The v0.5/v0.6 steps only rewrote a steering/correction rule that was already present, so 6 stores whose rubric.yml predated that rule (lumr, lief, Butterfly-Guide, Market-Analyzer, security, the Documents pebbl clone) never gained it — friction/regression/parked entries there fell through to no match and needed a manual --cat forever. Upgrade was reporting 'rubric.yml already up to date' over the gap, which is why it went unnoticed across a full 17-repo rollout.

the v0.4 ^trace: insertion anchored on the literal text [session], which never matches a rubric whose pattern is escaped as ^\[session\] — indexOf returned -1, the insert point collapsed to the first blank line, and the rule was written ABOVE the rules: key. pebbl's lenient hand-rolled parser reads such a rule anyway, so nothing broke visibly and 4 stores carried invalid YAML that any real parser would reject. Fixed by anchoring every insertion through insertRule (always below rules:, and below the [session] rule so it keeps first-match) plus a v0.8 repair step that moves stray rules back under the key.

rule ORDER is load-bearing in rubric.yml and insertions must respect it: the [session] rule has to stay above the unanchored keyword rules, or a session dump merely mentioning 'regression' classifies as steering instead of staying fleeting. First-match-wins makes any insertion anchor a behavioural decision, not a formatting one — my first pass at the v0.7 fix inserted correctly-shaped rules in the wrong position and demoted [session] in 4 stores before the anchor was fixed and the stores re-migrated.

R4 identity-keyed assert landed (schema v0.8, TEST-FIRST, uncommitted): 'pebbl log --key <identity>' makes a repeat assert COUNT instead of duplicating — a key with a live row (valid_to IS NULL) gets occurrences+1 and NO new db row and NO manual-logs.md append; identity is scoped to live beliefs so a superseded key is free again; --corrects is excluded because 'the belief changed' is not 'the same fact again'. Plus 'pebbl log --outcome failed|worked' (closed set, refused otherwise) which readback now LEADS with ('ALREADY TRIED — did NOT work'), so failure memory reaches a builder instead of dying in the store. New 'reassert' event type folds into the live row's count; a reassert with no live row folds to nothing (compaction supersedes entries by appending, so a dangling reassert is the steady state, not an anomaly). GOTCHA FOUND: parseArgs KNOWN_FLAGS is a closed allow-list — an unregistered flag is demoted to POSITIONAL and silently glued onto the message, so --key/--outcome had to be registered in src/args.js or the value vanished into the entry text. SECOND GOTCHA: readback's matchRows builds a throwaway in-memory FTS table with an explicit column list and re-reads rows from it, so any NEW logs column arrives as undefined downstream — R4 reads outcome/occurrences off the ORIGINAL row by index instead. Evidence: 19 new tests in test/idempotent-assert.test.js green, full suite 628/628, and four separate neuters (dedup branch off / dedup made unconditional / reassert removed from KNOWN_TYPES / readback outcome nulled) each turned them red, so they bite. Verified on a copy of the live loom store: 320 rows and newest timestamp unchanged after migrate, all defaults intact, and 3 keyed asserts collapsed to 1 row with occurrences=3.

COMPACTION ROLLUPS POISON RETRIEVAL (measured 2026-07-30, new eval harness at eval/readback-recall, committed 32e6ab6). On a 261-row snapshot of loom's store, 8 of 10 eval queries return a compaction ROLLUP at rank 1. Rollups are 5 of 261 rows (1.9%) but run 25k/30k/37k/114k/185k chars against a 1034-char MEDIAN entry — up to 179x. A row holding a quarter of accumulated text shares tokens with nearly any query, so bm25 puts it first and buries the specific precedent readback exists to surface. They COMPOUND: rollup headers nest on every pass ('steering notes on loom-maintain (2026-Q3): steering notes on loom-maintain (2026-Q3): ...'), so each compaction cycle makes the row bigger and the poisoning worse. COUNTERFACTUAL, measured: removing the 20 rollup-producing supersede events yields a LARGER 796-row corpus on which artifact-named recall@1 goes 0.20 -> 1.00 and MRR 0.533 -> 1.000 — every query returns its exact target first. Recall improved on a 3x bigger haystack, which rules out 'fewer rows, easier task'. FIX SHAPE: exclude or down-weight rollup rows as readback candidates (a rollup is a storage artifact, not a precedent a builder can act on); alternatively stop nesting rollup headers so a re-rolled bucket does not accumulate. NOT DONE HERE deliberately: loom's collision gate is being actively reworked in another session and changing readback ranking underneath it would collide. CAVEAT stated in BASELINE.md: dropping the supersedes also un-hides the rolled-up sources, so the counterfactual models 'never compacted' rather than 'ignore rollup rows'; a readback-side row filter would isolate it exactly.

migrate-to-events SILENTLY DROPS the liveness side-channel, and its output does not say so. Rehearsed 2026-07-30 on a full copy of loom's store before touching the real one. The migration lifts db.sqlite (logs + commits + handoffs) into a fresh canonical events.jsonl and moves the P0 tracer aside as events.tracer.bak.jsonl — correctly additive for everything db.sqlite holds. But liveness registrations and heartbeats exist ONLY as events (there is no liveness table in db.sqlite), so they are not lifted and the .bak is not read. MEASURED on the copy: event types went liveness-register 91 -> 1 and heartbeat 188 -> 1, and 'pebbl liveness check' went from 4 registered jobs to 2. Concretely lost: loom-maintain (every 1d, grace 6h, 84 heartbeats) and dev-tools-memory (every 24h, grace 12h, 3 heartbeats) — loom-maintain is the silent-failure detector for the maintenance plane, so migrating quietly blinds the thing that notices the custodian has stopped running. RECOVERY IS CHEAP AND VERIFIED: re-run 'pebbl liveness register <name> --every <d> --grace <g>' per job after migrating; registry returned to 4 jobs on the copy with no false OVERDUE, because registration seeds a fresh window. FIX SHAPES for the migrator itself: (a) carry liveness-register/heartbeat events across from the tracer into the new canonical log (they are already events — no lifting needed, just retention); or (b) at minimum, print a LOUD post-migration warning naming every liveness job that will need re-registering, the way --repair already warns about altered FK refs. (a) is correct; the migration claims to be additive and this is the one place it is not. CHECKABLE: a test that a store with N liveness-register events still reports N jobs from 'liveness check' after --apply.

migrate-to-events --apply --repair RAN ON THE REAL loom store 2026-07-30 and matched the rehearsal exactly. Reconciles: 264 append + 1 correct = the 265 logs, 33 commit, 5 handoff-open events in the new canonical events.jsonl; --repair backfilled all 33 commits-row FK refs from git (legacy-db.sqlite had commits=0) and wrote repair-manifest.json. The predicted liveness loss happened as measured: loom-maintain and dev-tools-memory were dropped and the two documented re-register commands restored a 4-job registry, healthy, no false OVERDUE (liveness-check self-registers on the next check, which is why recovery is two commands and not three). The jobs come back as never-beat-within-grace — registration seeds a fresh window, and loom-maintain's next 4h launchd run beats well inside 1d+6h, so the reset beat history raises no alarm. ONE THING THAT LOOKS LIKE A BUG AND IS NOT: the migration/doctor recreate an EMPTY db.sqlite (0/0/0 rows) beside the 1.1MB view.sqlite projection. That is the known compaction-safe pattern store-mode.js documents — mode is keyed on .events-canonical + legacy-db.sqlite presence, NOT on db.sqlite being absent. Verified storeMode('/Users/ashley/loom/.pebbl') === 'events'; search and doctor both read the full history. Do not file the empty db.sqlite as a defect.

GitHub push to SkywrightAI/pebbl 403s from the AshleyxAdamson fine-grained PAT because that token's Resource owner is the personal account, not the org. The repo checkboxes and Contents:Read-and-write in the token UI look correct but apply only to personal repos, so no org approval request is ever generated and the org's pending_requests page 404s. Diagnosis: the token reads exactly 3 AshleyxAdamson/* private repos and 404s on SkywrightAI private repos (GitHub returns 404, not 403, for repos a token has no grant on). Workaround that works today: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user newpathai) git push. Real fix: new fine-grained PAT with Resource owner set to SkywrightAI.

The pre-push public-repo hard gate deadlocks: it blocks until 'pebbl audit-history' is clean, but audit-history scans ALL committed history across git log --all. Once any finding lands in a commit already on the public remote, the scan can never go clean without rewriting published history, so the gate blocks every future push forever. Observed 2026-07-30: 8 findings, all in two already-pushed commits touching notes/design-event-sourcing-2026-06-17.md. Six are credential file PATHS, not credentials, and the file is the design doc that SPECIFIES the scanner, so it flags its own spec. Operator had to PEBBL_SKIP_SCAN=1 to push 9 unrelated commits. Risk: a gate that must be skipped every time trains the operator to always skip it, which is worse than no gate. Proposed fix: an accept-ledger keyed by finding fingerprint (file+commit+class+match) so ACCEPTed historical findings stop blocking and the gate only hard-blocks NEW findings in unpushed commits.

Droplet exposure from the audit-history network findings, checked 2026-07-30: the host is UP and SSH/22 is open, but the flagged app port is CLOSED (connection refused) - the dad-review service it pointed at is no longer running. So the leaked host:port in public history now resolves to a dead service. Residual risk is the bare droplet IP being discoverable in a public repo with SSH listening; mitigation is SSH hardening (key-only auth, fail2ban), not redaction, since the history is already published and cannot be un-leaked. Raw IP:port deliberately omitted from this entry to avoid re-leaking it into the committed log; see the audit-history output for the value.

Its main is a PROTECTED branch; the mechanism chosen was adding AshleyxAdamson to the repo's 'Allow specified actors to bypass required pull requests' list (classic branch protection rule, edit the EXISTING rule - creating a new one would leave two rules both applying to main). Fine-grained PAT repo creation: needs Repository permissions > Administration: Read and write AND repository access set to ALL repositories - a repo that does not exist yet cannot be in a 'selected repositories' list, which is why selecting repos individually can never enable creation. Granted 2026-07-30 to unblock creating SkywrightAI/frontend-loop. TRADEOFF NOW STANDING: Administration write across all org repos also permits rename, transfer, visibility change and DELETE on every repo, for as long as the token lives. Worth narrowing back to selected-repos + no Administration once repo creation is no longer needed. Note the account role is separate from the token: AshleyxAdamson's token failed with 'does not have the correct permissions' (an ACCOUNT-role error) while newpathai's failed with 'Resource not accessible by personal access token' (a TOKEN-scope error) - two different walls that look similar from the CLI.

MISTAKE + RECOVERY 2026-07-30: cleared 10.4GB of regenerable build output across projects, then reinstalled pebbl's deps with 'npm install' - wrong, because this repo is pnpm-only and its own .gitignore says so explicitly ('pnpm is the single source of truth... Do not let npm install re-add its lockfile'). Consequences: package.json rewritten (caret range pinned), package-lock.json created, better-sqlite3 native binding unbuilt, 233 of 705 tests failing. RECOVERY that worked: git checkout package.json pnpm-lock.yaml (a later pnpm install had ALSO bumped better-sqlite3 9.6.0 -> 11.10.0 in both manifests, so both needed reverting), then 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile' to install exactly the pinned 9.6.0 without letting pnpm rewrite anything. A node-gyp ENOENT on build/node_gyp_bins was fixed by mkdir -p on that exact path, not by deleting node_modules. THE STORE WAS NEVER AT RISK - events.jsonl is plain text and untouched by any of it; only the CLI's ability to READ it broke. LESSON: check the package manager a repo declares (packageManager field, pnpm-workspace.yaml, lockfile present) before running any install; --frozen-lockfile is the install that cannot rewrite manifests.

--relates was a silent no-op in any events-canonical store, fixed on branch fix/relates-link (commit df33a62).

ROOT CAUSE: 'pebbl log --relates N' wrote logs.relates_to into db.sqlite and stopped there. It never reached events.jsonl. In an events store that file is the source and db.sqlite is a rebuildable projection, so the relation was invisible to every read (view.sqlite showed relates_to NULL even immediately after the write) and vanished on the next rebuild. The command reported success throughout. MEASURED on a scratch --shared store: db.sqlite had relates_to=1, the event line had no relates_to key at all, and view.sqlite had NULL before and after 'pebbl rebuild'.

WHAT MADE IT INVISIBLE FOR SO LONG: the read side was already complete. fold.js line ~180 reads 'relates_to' off the event and line ~425 translates the eid back to a local int. Everything downstream was waiting for a field the writer never sent, so nothing errored — the feature just quietly did nothing.

TWO COMPANION DEFECTS, same surface: (1) the local integer id was UNDISCOVERABLE. 'pebbl help entry-ids' promises an id 'printed at log time' and says to find it via search or context; none of the three printed one, so there was no way to learn the number the flag demanded. (2) --relates/--corrects rejected eids via assertIntegerFlags, so the identity actually carried in events.jsonl — the only one that means the same entry in another clone — was the one form guaranteed to fail.

FIX: a present-only relatesField() tail on the append AND correct event makers (matching the sourceField/assertFields idiom, so an entry without a relation serializes byte-for-byte as before); a shared resolveEntryRef() that takes a local int OR an eid and resolves inside the store lock; assertEntryRefFlags replacing assertIntegerFlags for the two link flags; #id printed at log time and in search.

SUBTLETY WORTH KEEPING: the id printed at log time must be the FOLD's, not db.sqlite's lastInsertRowid. A migrated store has an empty db.sqlite beside a full event log, so the counters sit far apart — on a copy of this store the new entry was #82 by the fold and rowid 1 by the db. Printing the db id would hand out a ref resolving to the wrong entry.

VERIFIED: 8 new tests in test/relates-link.test.js, 3 of which fail with the fix reverted; full suite 713 pass / 0 fail; and a real linked entry landed in lumr's store carrying --corrects and --relates together.
